links.note: Two versions of the same promise: obtaining what one thinks of is easy if one keeps thinking of it (540), and if one is firm (666). The first asks for attention to be sustained, and the second for action to be.

25 calls Indra sufficient witness to the power of the one who controls the senses. Parimelazhagar makes 899's வேந்தன் Indra as well. The Kural itself only names Indra in 25, so the connection depends on his gloss.

203 calls refraining from harm even to enemies the height of understanding, and 261 defines austerity by harmlessness. Yet 264 advertises the power to crush foes. Parimelazhagar's 'enemies of virtue' and his comment that ascetics don't think of it are attempts to close this gap.

528 tells a king not to look at all alike but by rank; 541 says to show no favour to anyone. Household management and the court of justice have different requirements, though they are in consecutive chapters.
Both turn on அற்றம். Understanding is the inner fort against it, and one's own fault is the enemy that brings it. So the attacker and the defence are both within.

300 finds nothing better than truthfulness, while 323 puts not killing first and truthfulness right behind it. The Kural declares its rankings chapter by chapter, and here it comes close to correcting itself.

Two different conquests of death: by the power of austerity in 269, and by the vow of not killing in 326, where death's advance doesn't reach. The Kural offers an ethical route alongside the ascetic one.

1191 calls requited love the stoneless fruit, the ideal of enjoyment with nothing in the way. 1306 says love without quarrels is fruit gone bad or not yet ripe. So the obstacle that 1191 wishes away, 1306 says is what makes the fruit ripe.

434 calls one's own fault the only enemy that brings ruin. 448 shows the mechanism: without those who rebuke, no outside enemy is needed. Self-correction turns out to be something a person needs other people for.

201 makes fear the mark of the excellent; 1075 makes fear the conduct of the base. They can be reconciled only by asking what is feared, which suggests that fear of the deed and fear of the penalty are morally different things.

Just ten verses apart, this one ends the section on renunciation by promising a nature that can't be shifted, once craving goes. 380 asks what is stronger than fate, which gets there first. The Kural moves from the highest claim for human release straight to the strongest claim against human power.

வன்கண் is the same word in both. In 1156 he is hard because he could speak of leaving. In 1198 she calls herself hard for going on living without a word from him. The accusation has moved from him to her.

1041 says nothing is more painful than poverty except poverty itself. 558 names something more painful: wealth under a tyrant. The later chapter's superlative doesn't hold in this one's political conditions.
Both turn on தன்னைத்தான், making care for the self the argument for restraint: from evil deeds here, from anger in 305.

The wife lives within her husband's income, and 478 applies the same rule to the king's treasury: a small inflow is no ruin if outflow doesn't widen. The Kural's household economics and statecraft share one rule.
549 clears the king: punishing crime is no blemish but his work. 567 marks where that clearance ends, since punishment past the limit becomes a file on his own strength.

Both warn against telling pain to those not attuned to it. In 877 it is a matter of strategy and self-respect, and in 1200 the lover scolds her own heart for telling sorrow to one who doesn't care. The advice carries across books, and it is much sadder in the second one.

223 says that giving before a poor man can utter 'I have nothing' is found only in the well-born. 955 takes the giver's own means shrinking, and holds his nature constant. Giving is the chapter's real measure of lineage in both.
In 1130 she uses 'he lives within me' to refute the town's gossip. In 1249 she uses the same fact against her own heart, to stop it from leaving. The argument that once consoled her now traps her.

366 warns the renunciant to fear craving (அவா), because it deceives. In 1310, the sulking man names the same craving as what drives his heart to her. He uses the moral vocabulary correctly, with no intention of following it.
972 says standing differs because of deeds, and 505 makes deeds the touchstone. Together they offer a test of worth that doesn't refer to birth, and this is at odds with 502, three verses earlier.
They give the same rule different grounds. 206 rests on what will come back to you, 316 on knowing from your own experience what hurts. One argues from consequence and the other from fellow-feeling.

Both use பேராண்மை. Here the word is first attached to fierceness in battle. In 148 the great manhood is not looking at another's wife. The Kural contests what manhood is, and 773's own turn to helping the fallen foe is partway to 148.

706 says the face shows what is in the heart, as crystal shows what is next to it, in the chapter on reading signs in court. 1273 uses crystal the same way, with a thread inside it. Courtier and lover both depend on the transparency of the surface.
Both use the leaning staff, but 414 has listening as the staff and 415 the speaker's conduct. Read together, the staff only holds if the one speaking has conduct.

444 calls greater people as support the chief of all strengths; 497 says no support is needed but fearlessness, if the thinking and place are right. A chapter later, the book seems to take back its own superlative.

959 says that speech reveals lineage as a sprout reveals soil. 1044 shows the signal failing: poverty brings degraded speech out of the well-born. Speech is a sign of poverty as well as lineage, so the test is less reliable than chapter 96 claims.
The soul's hold on the body is the simile for virtue's bond in both: in 73 love's tie is like that of life to bone, and in 1013 worth holds on to shame in the same way.

1103 asks whether the Lotus-eyed one's world is sweeter than sleeping on the arms of one's beloved. 1323 repeats the challenge to heaven with a stranger choice: it's the quarrel that outdoes heaven now. Between these two verses, love has come to value its own frictions most.
278 shows the bathers with impure minds, and 298 states the principle that this water only reaches the body. Read together, the chapter on hypocrisy provides the case for this general claim.

positions.position: துணைமை is having the foreign court's ministers as support, which can calm a king's anger.
positions.quote: தமக்கு அவரமைச்சர் துணையாந்தன்மையும்

positions.position: The woman answers the friend who says that he will come: what use, if my own heart has already broken?
positions.quote: இது வருவா ரென்ற தோழிக்குத் தலைமகள் கூறியது.

positions.position: To cover a fault means to get rid of it. Covering the lesser thing while leaving the greater and thinking oneself decent is the folly.
positions.quote: குற்றம் மறைத்தலாவது, அவற்றை இலவாக்குதல்.

positions.position: The weak in view are those who don't respect one, which narrows the rule.
positions.quote: தம்மைப் போற்றாத எளியார்மாட்டுப் பகைகோடலை மேவுக

positions.position: Those striving are ascetics trying to give up the senses, and the householder gets the result without such effort.
positions.quote: புலன்களை விட முயல்வார் எல்லாருள்ளும் மிக்கவன்.

positions.position: He leaves deliberation to his ministers without sharing it, then rages at them when it fails, and they withdraw from him in fear.
positions.quote: அமைச்சர்மேல் வைத்து அவரோடு தானும் எண்ணிச் செய்யாத அரசன்

positions.position: It is being shaken by degrading attacks made on oneself.
The poverty returns across lives, birth after birth.
positions.quote: அத் தீவினையால் பிறவிதோறும் இலன் ஆம் என்பதாம்.

positions.position: The comparison is about being born a woman, which nothing exceeds if it has this firmness.
positions.quote: பெண் பிறப்புப்போல் மேம்பட்டன யாவையுள்?

positions.position: It is a tribute: death itself hesitates, in awe.
The name's reason restricts it to those with such grace, namely those in renunciation.
positions.quote: அந்தணரென்று சொல்லப்படுவார் துறவறத்தில் நின்றவர்.

positions.position: 'That too' is renunciation, which is good only if it is free of hypocrisy.
positions.quote: ஏனைத் துறவறமோ எனின், அதுவும் பிறனால் பழிக்கப்படுவது இல்லையாயின்

positions.position: The suffering is that of both, giver and receiver.
The woman speaks to her friend, who has seen her shoulders waste.
positions.quote: பிரிவிடை யாற்றாளாகிய தலைமகள் தனது தோள் வாட்ட முற்றது கண்ட தோழிக்குச் சொல்லியது.

positions.position: The parts are each person's own station, so what is due varies with position.
positions.quote: அவரவர் நிலைமைப்பகுதியோடே அறத்தின் பாற்பட்டு ஒழுகப் பெறுமாயின்,

positions.position: The one meant is any person greater in knowledge, and the failing is a lack of humility before such people.
The man speaks as he sets out to read her intent.
positions.quote: தலைமகள் குறிப்பறிதல் உற்றான் சொல்லியது.

positions.position: What is given up is wealth and pleasure that would reduce one's nature, however great the amount.
positions.quote: இது பொருளும் இன்பமும் மிகினும், தன்மை குறைவன் செய்யற்க

positions.position: Walls and door-guards are useless without நிறை, the holding of her heart to chastity.
positions.quote: காவல் இரண்டினும் நிறைக் காவல் இல்வழி ஏனைச் சிறைக்காவலால் பயன் இல்லை

positions.position: Those who truly investigate won't believe in rebirth at all, which reverses the claim into a denial of the doctrine.
One needs தவம் from an earlier birth, which gives the familiarity needed to complete it.
positions.quote: தவந்தானும் உண்டாவது முன்தவம் உடையார்க்கே

positions.position: Resting means total commitment: fixing mind, speech and body on the task while marching.
positions.quote: எப்பொழுதும் மன, மொழி, மெய்களை அதன் கண் வைத்துப் பகைமேல் செல்லும் அரசர்க்கு;

positions.position: இனம் means one's friends, who bring one ashore from a sea of sorrow.
positions.quote: தன்னைக் கரையேற விடுகின்ற நட்டோராகிய புணையைச் சுடும்.

positions.position: It is hypocrisy within one person, who is base while acting good.
The man tells the friend that she has hidden from him out of a false fear, and the cure is for the friend to explain that he isn't leaving.
positions.quote: என்கண் இல்லாத தொன்றனை உட்கொண்டு அது காரணமாக என்னை மறைத்துப் போன குறிப்பு

positions.position: வேந்து அமைவு is mutual: the people's love for the king and his grace toward them.
positions.quote: குடிகள் அவன்மாட்டு அன்புடையராதலும், அவன்தான் இவர்மாட்டு அருளுடையனாதலும் அடங்கின.

positions.position: These are ministers. He takes the verse's general word to refer to them, leaving priests to 441.
positions.quote: இது மந்திரிகளைக் கூட் மாறு கூறிற்று.

positions.position: All are equal by birth, and difference appears only in the skill shown at one's work.
The esteemed one is honoured by chaste women, and கெழீஇயிலர் means she lacks good deeds, that is, she has bad karma.
positions.quote: கெழீஇயின்மை; நல்வினையின்மை

positions.position: மானம் is the pride of asking 'why must I alone suffer while the rest are comfortable?'
positions.quote: 'இக்குடியிலுள்ளார் யாவரும் இன்பமுற இக்காலத்துத் துன்பமுறுவேன் யானோ?'
